newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tunisia holds suspects in Belgian political murder.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia holds suspects in Belgian political murder.

text.p: Tunisian police have arrested two Tunisians suspected of shooting dead leading Belgian politician Andre Cools more than five years ago, the Belgian foreign ministry said on Thursday.

"Our ambassador (in Tunis) has received information (from Tunisian Justice Minister Sadok Chaabane) about two Tunisians who have been arrested in connection with the murder of Cools," a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
In Tunis, sources close to the investigation said the two had admitted assassinating Cools, one-time kingmaker of the Socialist Party, in a mafia-style murder.

The sources identified the suspects as Abdelmajid el-Almi and Abdeljelil Ben Brahim and said they had confessed to being given a contract for the killing by a European while they were living in Europe.
Cools, a former Socialist minister, was shot at point-blank range in the car park outside his mistress's appartment near the eastern Belgian city of Liege on July 18, 1991.
The ministry said Tunisia normally did not extradite its nationals, which would make it unlikely the two will stand trial in Belgium.
But the spokesman said Belgium and Tunisia planned to coordinate their actions.
Belgian teletext said the two men were hired in Sicily with the help of the local mafia.
Six people, including former government minister Alain Van der Biest, have been arrested and charged with orchestrating Cools's murder. Van der Biest denies any involvement in the killing.
It is not known who ordered the murder or why, although the crime has been linked to an announcement by Cools that he would make revelations about corruption in the francophone Socialist party.
According to lawyers for some of the accused, witnesses told investigators the murder was a contract killing for 750,000 Belgian francs ($25,000).
Over the past five years the inquiry into Cools's death and his role in the top ranks of the Socialist Party has uncovered corruption at the highest levels of Belgian government.
The scandal has led to the resignation of four ministers and NATO Secretary General Willy Claes and the suicide of a top general.
